quote: Five science teachers were purposefully selected to generate and implement adaptive learning pathways for IBL instruction.
rationale: Teachers use the generative AI to create lesson pathways, so it is not learner-facing (E1, the first applicable code). The study is also a qualitative case study with teacher interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Employing a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design, this research measures mathematical reasoning (MR) and critical thinking (CT) using validated instruments with inter-rater reliability of 0.89.
rationale: The abstract describes a quasi-experiment with 240 secondary students in mathematics, comparing LLM-assisted and human-AI collaborative learning against traditional instruction, and measures mathematical reasoning quantitatively. Publication type (journal), SMD data sufficiency, and full-text language cannot be judged from the abstract, and they are not shown to fail, so the record advances to full text.

quote: We surveyed 297 STEM undergraduates at a single English-medium Sino–UK joint institution to document perceptions of AI chatbots for learning.
rationale: This is a cross-sectional descriptive survey of perceptions. It has no control group without generative AI, and it is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design. It reports only perceptions, with no learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order, because the abstract does not show that the chatbots were the learner-facing intervention of a learning activity.

quote: empirical evidence from a quasi-experimental study conducted with 151 first-year computer science students
rationale: The abstract describes a quasi-experimental study of first-year computer science students using generative AI tools, with performance outcomes in programming. The comparison group is not explicit, and the venue and publication type are not given, but nothing shows a criterion failing, so the record advances to full text for those checks.

quote: This study investigates the integration of AI chatbots in Home Economics instruction in secondary schools, focusing on teaching practices, student perceptions, and learning outcomes within a rural Philippine context.
rationale: The content domain is Home Economics, which is not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science, so the domain criterion fails. E2 is the first applicable exclusion code in order; comparison and design are unclear but do not change the decision.

quote: Design: descriptive cross-sectional survey in one large public school.
rationale: The study is a single-group descriptive survey with no control group that goes without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. It also reports only student perceptions from a questionnaire. E3 is the first applicable code in order, since the intervention (students using ChatGPT) appears learner-facing and the STEM content is not clearly ruled out.

quote: randomly assigned by class to the experimental group ( N = 48, using a GenAI-based chatbot) and the control group ( N = 49, using a search engine)
rationale: Primary students in a science inquiry activity used a GenAI chatbot, and a search-engine control group (a non-AI tool) was compared in a quasi-experiment. Problem posing ability is a quantitative skill outcome, and the abstract reports group sizes and t-values. Nothing in the abstract shows a failed criterion; the journal, date and English abstract are consistent with eligibility, and data sufficiency and full-text language are left for full text.

quote: investigate the effect of using MATLAB application that provides users with convenient access to OpenAI's ChatGPT (MatGPT) on mathematical proficiency among undergraduate students enrolled in the Differential Equation Course.
rationale: Undergraduates use a ChatGPT-based tool in a differential equations course, in a quasi-experiment with a traditional-teaching control group and a quantitative proficiency test. Data sufficiency, English full text and journal article status are not contradicted at the abstract stage and can be checked at full text.

quote: Utilizing GPT-4, a high school mathematics teaching plan dataset was generated. Finally, the performance of LLMs in instructional design was evaluated.
rationale: GPT-4 was used by researchers to generate teaching plans that were then evaluated, so no learner interacts with generative AI (AI used only for teacher or researcher preparation, E1). The abstract also describes no control group, no student participants, and no learning outcome.

quote: Nine independent instructors from 5 centers, who were blinded to the source of the scenarios (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, NRP® and RETAIN), evaluated the performance of scenarios using modified Jeffries Simulation Design Scale (JSDS).
rationale: LLMs were used only to generate scenarios that instructors rated, so no learner interacted with generative AI (E1, the first applicable code). The content is also neonatal resuscitation, a health professions topic, and there is no learner learning outcome.

quote: a quasi-experimental study was conducted in a high school in East China, involving 100 first-year students in a three-week Python course, where the experimental group adopted the GAI-supported programming teaching model (n = 52), and the control group followed the traditional programming teaching model (n = 48).
rationale: Quasi-experiment with a non-AI control group, high school students, Python programming, and a quantitative programming performance outcome all appear met. Journal article from 2026. Statistics sufficiency and full-text language are not judged at the abstract stage and are left for full text.

quote: Exploring the impact of persona-based large language models on user experience in educational settings
rationale: The record has no abstract, so there is no positive evidence that any criterion fails. The title suggests a learner-facing LLM but also a focus on user experience (possibly perceptions only), and it gives no information on STEM domain, comparison group, design or learning outcomes. The record cannot be excluded at this stage and should be resolved at full text.

quote: This paper explores the role of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4, in grading processes in higher education and compares their effectiveness with that of traditional human grading methods.
rationale: The LLM is used only for grading scripts, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, which the protocol excludes (E1). The study compares AI marks with human marks and has no learner groups or learning outcomes.

quote: A quantitative quasi-experimental method with a nonequivalent pretest–posttest control group design was applied to 64 eighth-grade students
rationale: Generative AI use by learners, a conventional-instruction control group, a quasi-experimental design, secondary students and a quantitative critical thinking test all appear to be met. The abstract never names the subject taught, so it is unclear whether the content is STEM, and missing information is not grounds to exclude. Resolve the domain, and whether the effect-size data are sufficient, at full text.

quote: the study administered a descriptive–correlational survey to 60 randomly selected students and used short interviews and open-ended responses to contextualize the quantitative results.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey of self-reported generative AI use, with no control group and no experimental or quasi-experimental design. The outcomes are perceived benefits and self-reported performance. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: General Background Educational transformations in the digital era increasingly leverage automated technologies to create interactive and adaptive instruction within language learning contexts.
rationale: The content is environmental poster writing in language classrooms, which is language learning and not STEM, so the domain criterion fails. The other criteria appear met (ChatGPT, non-equivalent control group, eleventh graders, learning outcome scores), but E2 applies first among the failed criteria.

quote: Pre-test and post-test evaluations were used to measure critical thinking (Watson-Glaser Critical Thinking Appraisal–Short Form) and sustainable learning skills (adapting the SSLSS for students).
rationale: Learner-facing ChatGPT/Gemini, a quasi-experimental control group, and secondary students all meet the criteria. The abstract names no STEM subject, and the outcomes are general critical thinking and a sustainable-learning-skills scale rather than clear STEM learning. Missing information is not grounds to exclude at the abstract stage, so this goes to full text to check the subject area and whether the outcomes count as learning measures.

quote: This study investigated the impact of AI-driven personalized learning pathways on the academic performance of medical students in acute abdomen topic, comparing against traditional learning method.
rationale: The content is acute abdomen in a general surgery course for undergraduate medical students. This is health professions education, which the protocol excludes under Domain, so E2 applies. The other criteria appear met (ChatGPT-4 intervention, randomized crossover with a control group, post-test scores reported).

quote: 컴퓨터공학과 2·3학년 학생 30명을 대상으로 한 학기 동안 오류 현상 확인, 관련 코드 영역 탐색, 오류 원인 분석, 수정 방향 탐색, 결과 검증의 5단계 피드백을 적용하였다.
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 30 computer engineering students who all received generative AI stepwise feedback, with no separate control group, and it analyzes problem-solving processes rather than a learning outcome. Language is not grounds for exclusion at this stage. The comparison failure is positive evidence, so E3 applies as the first applicable code in order (the missing quantitative learning outcome is a second, later failure).

quote: Sixty sixth-grade students from two complete classes were randomly assigned to either an experimental group engaged in AR science learning with a GPA-enhanced 5E approach or a control group that followed the traditional 5E method.
rationale: Sixth-graders learn science with generative AI pedagogical agents and are compared with a traditional 5E control group without generative AI. Academic achievement is measured. Data sufficiency, English full text and publication type (journal article, 2024) are not contradicted by the abstract and can be checked at full text.

quote: The results reveal significant performance differences, with AI demonstrating higher accuracy, faster response times, and greater consistency, particularly on essay-based problems requiring higher-order reasoning.
rationale: Secondary students used ChatGPT versus conventional instruction in a pretest-posttest control design in mathematics, so the other criteria appear met. The reported outcomes (accuracy, response time, consistency) seem to describe the AI's own performance rather than student learning gains, so it is unclear whether a quantitative learning outcome exists. This needs to be resolved at full text.

quote: confirming a clear initial gap in perceived AI literacy even among the majors
rationale: The study meets the other criteria: learner-facing Gemini, a nonequivalent control group, university students, and a programming course. However, every outcome is framed as perceived AI literacy (self-reported scale sub-factors), so the abstract gives positive evidence of a perception-only outcome and no quantitative measure of learning.

quote: presents the findings of a year-long experimental study in both types of classrooms. Our findings suggest that students generally found ChatGPT easy to use and beneficial to their learning, reporting improved confidence, motivation, and engagement.
rationale: Learners use ChatGPT in higher-education coding and physics activities, but the abstract reports only perceptions and compares activity types and student subgroups. It does not show whether there is a non-generative-AI control group or a quantitative learning outcome, and missing information is not grounds to exclude at abstract stage, so this goes to full text.

quote: This study employed a quasi-experimental design to explore the possible impact of ChatGPT-facilitated programming mode on college students' programming behaviors, performances, and perceptions.
rationale: College students used ChatGPT for programming, compared with a self-directed programming class without generative AI, in a quasi-experiment that measured programming performance. Data sufficiency, language and publication type are not judged at abstract stage and nothing in the record shows a failed criterion, so it advances to full text.

quote: This study explores high school students’ AI literacy and their use of ChatGPT in English language learning
rationale: The content is English language learning, which is non-STEM and explicitly excluded. The study is also a questionnaire-and-interview mixed-methods design with no control group and no learning outcome, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: a one-group pretest-posttest evaluation involving 60 fourth-grade students
rationale: The abstract states the study is a single-group pre-post design with no comparison group, which the protocol excludes under Comparison and the borderline rules map to E3. The other criteria (LLM chatbot, elementary mathematics, quantitative scores) appear met.

quote: the research evaluates the opportunities and challenges of integrating GenAI into mental health support services in school settings.
rationale: The study gathers qualitative perceptions of trust in GenAI chatbot therapists for school mental health support. It does not involve learners using a generative AI tool in a learning activity. It also has no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: A comparative analysis between experimental and control groups was conducted to determine the app's effectiveness. Findings revealed a statistically significant improvement in the performance of students using the application (p < 0.001)
rationale: Learners use a ChatGPT-based app for C# programming in higher education, with an experimental vs. control group comparison and a quantitative performance outcome. Nothing in the abstract shows a failed criterion. Randomization, the control condition's details, and whether data suffice for an SMD are not stated, so these are left for full text.

quote: this study aims to investigate the capability of GPT-4o, the versatile and flagship model by OpenAI, in characterising relational feedback and evaluate how its effectiveness varies across zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting strategies.
rationale: GPT-4o is used by researchers to classify feedback sentences, so learners do not interact with it, and the study compares only prompting strategies. The abstract also reports no learner outcome, and feedback classification is not STEM content. E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Following the PRISMA guidelines, 21 studies were selected from 79 preliminary items retrieved from the RISS and KCI databases.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of prior studies, not an empirical experiment or quasi-experiment, so it is not an eligible design or publication type. Under the exclusion code order, E6 (not an empirical study) applies.

quote: This critical posthuman work uses a professional learning scenario to ask questions about the historically present challenges of asking teachers to use GenAI as a universal good
rationale: The abstract describes a critical posthuman diffractive reading, which is a qualitative or theoretical design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The participants appear to be teachers in professional learning, not students. E3 is the first exclusion code in order that clearly applies.

quote: TeacherGen@i facilitates meaningful development of teaching competencies such as instructional decision-making, classroom communication, and student engagement
rationale: The content is teaching skills in teacher education, not STEM content, so E2 is the first code that applies. The study is also an explanatory case study that uses usability surveys and reflective journals, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Limitations include single-group design, small sample ( n = 22), immediate testing only, and keyword-based depth proxies.
rationale: The abstract states a single-group design in which 22 students completed a pre-test, an LLM-assisted task, and a post-test. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail (E3).

quote: content analysis of 60 LLM responses to standardized prompts reveals consistent coverage of technical competencies such as cloud computing and programming
rationale: The study is a content analysis of LLM outputs to prompts. No learners interact with a generative AI tool in a learning activity, and there are no student participants, no control group and no learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1.

quote: Using a one-group pretest-posttest design, 34 pre-/in-service teachers completed the module in 2025
rationale: The abstract reports a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group, so E3 applies first in the code order. The sample also includes in-service teachers, which would fail the population criterion, but E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: ChatGPT as a learning supervision assistant in the evaluation process of Lesson Plans (RPP) and Student Worksheets (LKPD)... helps teachers identify document weaknesses, provide alternative improvements, and expedite the supervision process
rationale: ChatGPT is used by teachers or supervisors to review lesson plans and worksheets, not by learners, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1, the first applicable code). The design is also descriptive qualitative, with no control group and no learning outcome.

quote: we conducted a survey among students. The results indicate a positive correlation between the use of our artificial intelligence tools and student exam performance
rationale: The abstract describes a survey with a correlation between tool use and exam performance. That is a correlational design with no separate non-generative-AI control group, which the protocol excludes. E3 is the first applicable code in order, since the ChatGPT intervention and the mathematics domain both qualify.

quote: This study assessed ChatGPT’s effectiveness in improving EFL learners’ sentence structure competence.
rationale: The content is English grammar, which is language learning and therefore not STEM. E2 is the first applicable code in order. The one-group pretest-posttest design would also fail the comparison and design criteria (E3).

quote: A Strategic Analysis of Generative Artificial Intelligence Simulated Client Role-Play Training in Rehabilitation Counseling Education
rationale: The index has no abstract, but the title shows the content is rehabilitation counseling education. That is a counseling and health-professions field, not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming or data science, so the domain criterion fails. The generative AI role-play is learner-facing, so E1 does not apply.

quote: Employing a quasi-experimental design, the research was conducted with 84 second-year computer science students at Azerbaijan State Pedagogical University over a 16-week semester.
rationale: Quasi-experiment with a non-AI control group, higher education computer science students using LLM assistants, and quantitative post-test learning outcomes. Published in a journal in 2026. Data sufficiency and full-text language are not determinable at abstract stage, so they are checked at full text.

quote: ChatGPT has been extensively tested for triage, translation, clinical workflow, consultation, medical research, medical education, and so on.
rationale: This is an editorial commentary on ChatGPT's performance on medical licensing exams and on publication trends. Learners do not interact with generative AI in a learning activity, and there is no control group, STEM domain, student population, or learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in the specified order, although the record would also fail E2 (health professions), E3, E4, E5, E6 and E10.

quote: Nurse educators are concerned about the erosion of students' accountability to learn rather than take shortcuts.
rationale: The record is a commentary on ChatGPT in nursing education, and its examples (nursing essays, a sepsis protocol) are health professions content, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. It also has no control group, no research design and no learning outcome, so E3 and E6 would apply too, but E2 comes first in the order.

quote: These findings support homework as complementary assessment evidence while showing that calendar-based comparisons cannot identify the educational effects of generative AI.
rationale: This is a retrospective correlational study of homework and exam scores across cohorts. No learners interacted with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails. E1 is the first applicable code in order, though the design is also correlational and there is no AI-free control group.

quote: The AI system's adaptive algorithms successfully identified knowledge gaps in 78% of learners, enabling targeted interventions.
rationale: The design is a quasi-experiment with a conventional-teaching control, and undergraduates took pre- and post-tests. The 'AI-based adaptive platforms' may be non-generative, and no subject domain is stated; the closing mention of STEM as future research hints it may not be STEM. Neither is positive evidence of failure, so this is advanced to full text.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed, dividing participants into two groups: a control group utilizing traditional scaffolding methods and an experimental group integrating GAI tools alongside scaffolding techniques.
rationale: A quasi-experiment with a non-GAI control group in first-year university programming courses measures coursework and final project performance. The GAI toolset includes Notebook LM, which is generative, though Kahoot! and Slido are not. How far learners use the generative tools themselves and whether the statistics are sufficient should be checked at full text, but nothing in the abstract shows a criterion failing.

quote: The method used in this study is a literature review related to ChatGPT, gathered from the Google database using the Google Advanced search strategy.
rationale: The record is a literature review with no participants, no control group and no learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order, because the abstract gives no positive evidence that E1 or E2 applies. The record is also not an empirical study (E6).

quote: This quasi-experimental study compared GenAI-supported flipped learning (AI-FL) with reading-based flipped learning (R-FL) in an 11-week preservice chemistry course.
rationale: Learners use GenAI in pre-class learning, and the comparison is an intact reading-based class with no GenAI, so this is a quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Participants are preservice chemistry teachers (higher education), and lesson-design performance is a rubric-based, pretest-adjusted skill outcome. Whether the statistics suffice for an effect size cannot be judged from the abstract, so this is left for full text.

quote: the experimental group, which adopted the new approach, significantly outperformed the control group, which used GenAI without restrictions
rationale: Both groups used generative AI: the experimental group followed a structured GenAI approach and the control group used GenAI without restrictions. The protocol excludes studies that only compare two generative AI variants, and there is no non-GenAI control group.

quote: This quasi-experimental study with the pretest-post-test non-equivalent group design involved 47 subjects, 24 in the experimental group and 23 in the control group.
rationale: Quasi-experiment with a control group, university mathematics education students, and PBL with ChatGPT as the intervention. Critical thinking is measured quantitatively with pre- and post-test means reported. Whether the control group avoided generative AI, the standard deviations available for the effect size, and the full-text language are not shown in the abstract, so these are left for full-text screening.

quote: we conducted a mixed-methods case study involving a focal teaching intervention with 49 students and an evaluation study with 36 in-service teachers. The students' pre- and post-tests indicate statistically significant learning gains
rationale: The student component is a single group measured with pre- and post-tests and no separate control group, which the protocol and borderline rules treat as E3. The AI is mainly used by teachers to generate materials, and the teacher evaluation sample is in-service teachers, so nothing else in the abstract could make the record eligible.

quote: We compared two pedagogical approaches: GAI‐Scaffolded Learning (GSL), where GPT employs structured Socratic dialogue to guide problem‐solving and GAI‐Direct Learning (GDL), which provides immediate answers without guided inquiry.
rationale: Both conditions use GPT (Socratic vs. direct-answer variants) and no group is described without generative AI, so the comparison fails under the protocol's rule against studies comparing only two generative AI variants. The outcomes described are behaviours, interaction patterns and perceptions rather than a learning measure.

quote: This quasi-experimental study examined the effectiveness of ChatGPT-assisted instruction in enhancing English proficiency among 60 engineering students at a Saudi university
rationale: The learning content and outcomes are English language proficiency (speaking and writing), which is language learning and therefore non-STEM, even though the participants are engineering students. The other criteria appear met, but the domain exclusion applies.

quote: The experimental group (n = 180) received AI-enhanced instruction using uLesson, PhET Interactive Simulations, and ChatGPT, while the control group (n = 180) was taught using conventional lecture-based methods.
rationale: A quasi-experiment with a non-equivalent control group compares SS2 students who used a bundle that includes ChatGPT against lecture-based instruction on a STEM achievement test. No criterion is positively failed. How students used ChatGPT within the bundle, and whether the reported statistics are enough for an SMD, should be checked at full text.

quote: This approach involves a combination of an open-ended survey and semi-structured interviews for high school and undergraduate students to holistically explore these facets.
rationale: The study is purely qualitative, using an open-ended survey and interviews. It has no control group without generative AI and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. The 'comparative perspective' contrasts academic fields, not AI and non-AI groups. E3 is the first applicable code in order, and the missing quantitative outcome (E5) would also fail.

quote: This study aims to see whether there is a significant influence on the writing ability of grade XI students after using ChatGPT at SMAN 1 Karangrejo.
rationale: The study measures EFL writing ability, which is language learning and not STEM content, so the domain criterion clearly fails. Other criteria (ChatGPT, control class, K-12 students) appear met, but E2 applies as the first failing code.

quote: The source code of 16 students from the control group (without ChatGPT) and 22 students from the treatment group (with ChatGPT) who completed identical programming exercises focused on coding conventions was analyzed.
rationale: Undergraduates in Java programming used ChatGPT versus a control group without it, with code quality measured by static analysis (a quantitative skill-performance measure). Whether assignment was random or the comparison group was quasi-experimental is not stated, and data sufficiency, English full text and publication type (IEEE Access journal, 2024) are not contradicted, so nothing gives positive evidence of failure at the abstract stage.

quote: This study surveyed 480 upper-secondary students (Grades 10 - 12) in Lao Cai province, Vietnam, to describe how they use AI tools in physics learning, how they self-assess their competence
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey with no control group and no experimental or quasi-experimental design. It reports only self-reported use and self-assessed competence, not a learning outcome. The generative AI tools are learner-facing, so E1 does not apply, and E3 is the first code that does.

quote: Survey data were collected from 153 undergraduate students. The questionnaire examined awareness of AI and automation, perceived risks to traditional entry-level work, anxiety and perceived preparedness
rationale: This is a perceptions survey of undergraduates. No learner-facing generative AI learning activity, control group, or quantitative learning outcome is described. E1 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: The aim of this study is to establish a baseline profile of selected predictors prior to the planned implementation of an AI assistant for self-study in mathematics.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based baseline survey run before any AI assistant was implemented, so no learner-facing generative AI intervention was delivered. It is correlational, has no control-group comparison, and has no learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: A cross-sectional correlational study examined 525 students from four academic strands.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional correlational survey of AI literacy and grades. No generative AI tool was assigned as a learning activity, so there is no intervention and no control group. E1 is the first applicable code in order, and the correlational design fails the design criterion as well.

quote: This study aimed to develop and examine the effect of an artificial intelligence chatbot educational program for promoting nursing skills related to electronic fetal monitoring in nursing college students
rationale: The abstract describes nursing education (electronic fetal monitoring), and the title refers to health professions educators. Health professions education is excluded by the Domain criterion. Whether the chatbot is generative is unclear, so E1 cannot be applied, but E2 is positively supported.

quote: This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools on the grammatical accuracy and vocabulary range of undergraduate ESL learners.
rationale: The content is ESL academic writing, which is language learning and explicitly excluded as non-STEM. The other criteria appear met: a randomized AI versus no-AI comparison in undergraduates, with the title naming generative AI. Domain alone fails, so the code is E2.

quote: This study aims to find out how far students use ChatGPT to help them learn Arabic
rationale: The content is Arabic language learning, which is not STEM and is explicitly excluded as language learning. E2 is the first applicable code in order. The study is also qualitative (observation, interviews), with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This study investigates the impact of AI-assisted task-based language teaching (TBLT) on the acquisition of academic English collocations in spoken discourse.
rationale: The content is academic English collocations, which is language learning and not STEM, so the domain criterion fails. Intervention, comparison, design, population and outcome otherwise appear met, but E2 is the first exclusion code that applies.

quote: This exploratory inquiry consolidates recent scholarly works to discuss the potential benefits and downsides of ChatGPT in terms of increasing teaching and learning.
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review or discussion paper that consolidates prior literature. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It also has no STEM focus. E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits this evidence.

quote: ChatGPT and Grammarly, which are AI-based writing assistants, for the English as Foreign Language Iraqi undergraduate students to improve academic writing.
rationale: The content is EFL academic essay writing, which is language learning and not STEM, so the domain criterion fails. E2 is the first applicable code in order. The study also appears to be a single-group pre-post case study with no control group, but E2 takes precedence.

quote: A descriptive, cross-sectional, non- experimental study was conducted with a purposive sample of 124 first-year Human Anatomy students from seven different health science programs.
rationale: The content is human anatomy taught to health science students, which is health professions education and is excluded from the STEM domain (E2, the first applicable code). The study is also a cross-sectional satisfaction survey with no control group and no learning outcome.

quote: Using secondary survey data from higher-education participants (N = 751), a three-item behavioral intention composite and a 0–7 usage-frequency index were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression.
rationale: This is a correlational survey of intention and self-reported ChatGPT use in a single sample. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order, since ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI and the abstract gives no positive evidence on STEM content.

quote: This study examined the effects of prompt engineering-based structured AI-assisted feedback on pre-service physics teachers’ inquiry-based science teaching self-efficacy and feedback literacy.
rationale: The intervention (ChatGPT-based feedback), the control group, the quasi-experimental design, the population (preservice teachers count as higher education) and the domain (physics) all meet the criteria. The only outcomes are self-efficacy and feedback literacy, measured by scales. These are affective or perceptual measures, not a quantitative measure of learning, so E5 applies.

quote: explore students’ perceptions of digital literacy and writing skills using an interactive multimedia platform based on Kapatu Mbojo local literature, integrated with Google Gemini
rationale: The content is writing skills and local literature taught by Indonesian language teachers, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. The abstract also suggests a pre-post design with no control group, but E2 is the first code in order that applies.

quote: this study analyzes the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) based language tools on improving students' spoken English fluency at Arifa Institute of Technology, Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu.
rationale: The learning content and outcome are spoken English fluency, pronunciation, and confidence, which is language learning and not STEM, and the protocol excludes language learning. The engineering student population does not make the content STEM.

quote: ChatGPT gave several correct answers to 20 questions but failed the test with 45%.
rationale: The researchers tested ChatGPT's own accuracy on 20 questions. No learners interact with it in a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1, the first code that applies). The abstract also shows no control group, no student sample, and no learning outcome, and the content is sports and exercise psychology rather than STEM.

quote: The study approached a quasi-experimental method with a single group of (42) female undergraduate students studying in courses related to designing electronic newspapers.
rationale: The abstract positively states a single-group design with no separate control group, so the comparison criterion fails (E3 per the single-group borderline rule). Domain (e-newspaper design in media) also appears non-STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: This study evaluated interactive oral assessments (IOA) as an alternative to traditional written examinations in bioscience education.
rationale: The intervention is an oral assessment format, not learner-facing generative AI. Generative AI is mentioned only as a possible source of academic misconduct that the format resists, so the intervention criterion clearly fails.

quote: These strategies aim to effectively facilitate language learning and academic writing for those who are learning English as a foreign language.
rationale: The content is English language learning and academic writing, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. The study is also a qualitative narrative inquiry of three students' perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: to facilitate the development of Englishspeaking competence, such as pronunciation, conversational fluency, and speaking confidence
rationale: The content is English speaking and pronunciation, which is language learning and excluded as non-STEM (E2, the first applicable code in order). The study is also a single-group pre-post design, which would fail E3 as well.

quote: quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test, and a control group. [...] Data collection tools included ChatGPT chatbots with Wolfram Alpha and ChemDraw plugins, and two researcher-made academic achievement tests on chemistry
rationale: Twelfth-grade chemistry students used ChatGPT versus a control group in a quasi-experiment with achievement pre/post tests, so all criteria appear met. Publication type, language, and whether the control group was non-AI and the data sufficient for an SMD are not stated, so these are left to full-text checking.

quote: students were systematically engaged with instructional texts generated by ChatGPT that contained intentionally embedded logical and factual errors

quote: This study address gap through a qualitative narrative inquiry into the lived experience of eighteen IT teachers working in Nepalese institutions.
rationale: The study is a qualitative narrative inquiry based on interviews with 18 IT teachers. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order. E4 and E5 also apply.

quote: we evaluated various NLP tools such as ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. We used them to solve typical problems in mechanical engineering to assess their reliability and accuracy.
rationale: The researchers ran the generative AI tools themselves on engineering problems to test accuracy, so learners did not interact with them. The abstract also says classroom implementation and effectiveness testing are future work, so there is no student comparison or learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Independent t-tests (p > 0.05) and negligible effect sizes (Cohen's d < 0.2) revealed no significant difference between technical (ICT) and non-technical (Physics) students.
rationale: All 50 students used the Llama 2 VR system, and the only group comparison is between ICT and Physics students, so there is no control group without generative AI (E3). The measured outcomes are system latency and ARCS motivation, which are not learning outcomes, so E5 would also apply, but E3 comes first in the order.

quote: This study aimed to evaluate the potential of AIGC to bridge the cancer knowledge gap, assessing the roles of health self-efficacy as a mediator and educational level as a moderator in this relationship.
rationale: The learning content is cancer and health knowledge, which is not STEM and is closer to health education. E2 is the first applicable code. The design is also a longitudinal survey of AIGC use frequency with no non-AI control group, which would fail E3 as well.

quote: we surveyed 330 secondary school students in China (Grades 7--11) about their preferred tutoring behaviors, attitudes toward proactive intervention, and acceptable use of learning-process data.
rationale: The abstract describes a preference and attitude survey. No generative AI intervention was delivered to learners, and there is no control group or learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code, and the survey design and perception-only outcomes also fail the protocol.

quote: SIGSOFT FSE Companion
rationale: The venue is the companion proceedings of a software engineering conference, and the protocol excludes conference proceedings. The other criteria look met or unclear: the checklist-only group is a non-AI comparison and the topic is unit testing, which is computer science. Publication type fails, so the record is excluded.

quote: To achieve this objective, we collected and analyzed articles from 2021 to 2024, and 72 studies were thoroughly examined.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not a primary empirical study with a control group, so it fails the design criterion and the publication type exclusion for reviews. Under the ordered codes, E6 (not an empirical study) is the first that applies, since E1–E5 cannot be positively judged for a review.
